messages:
omar: Heads up — customers are reporting small unexpected token charges when a client reconnects mid-stream and the server truncates an in-flight tool call. Looks like ~10-200 tokens per affected session, not catastrophic but reproducible. Anyone seen this in traces?

kevin: Yep, ran into one last week. quick gist from the trace: we get a toolcall_start (provisional +200), then client disconnect, resume with a new connection_id, we emit another provisional +150, then finalization only reconciles one of them.

kevin: Log snippet:```json
{
  "req_id": "r_94x",
  "events": [
    {"type":"stream_chunk","connection_id":"c-A","offset":0},
    {"type":"toolcall_start","tool":"search","tokens_prov":200,"prov_key":"prov:c-A:seq-42"},
    {"type":"disconnect","connection_id":"c-A"},
    {"type":"session_resume","new_connection_id":"c-B","req_meta":{"resume_from":42}},
    {"type":"toolcall_truncate","tool":"search","tokens_prov":150,"prov_key":"prov:c-B:seq-42"},
    {"type":"finalize","prov_keys":["prov:c-A:seq-42"]}
  ]
}
```

marta: Sounds like the core bug: provisional entries are keyed by connection_id. when the client rebinds with a different connection id we create a second provisional entry instead of updating the original. finalization picks one prov_key and the other stays provisional and counts toward the customer until reconciliation.

ben: Agree. We used connection_id because it's cheap and strictly scoped to the lifetime of a socket. But for resumable sessions we need a stable identifier. We could use client-sent `client_request_id` or `req_id` if present. If not present, we can fall back to a deterministic hash of the first N bytes of the prompt + model + route.

kevin: Two gotchas: 1) some legacy clients don't send request_id so we need backcompat; 2) fallback routing (route A failed -> route B) intentionally generates a new route id and we must avoid merging unrelated provisional entries that happen to have same prompt prefix.

oma­r: @kevin good points. We shouldn't merge across route boundaries. Proposed rule: prov_key = stable_request_token if available else connection_bound_key. For resumes where client supplies `req_id`, map both connection keys to the same prov_key and ensure finalization clears both provisional entries atomically.

sara: From console UX side this shows up as two provisional charge lines with different session ids and confusing timestamps. Short-term we can group provisional rows that share req_id or same prompt hash into one aggregated row with a tooltip explaining resume. That will reduce support noise.

marta: Implementation sketch: 1) runtime: accept optional `client_request_id` in the streaming handshake and propagate to all provisional ledger ops; 2) router: when resuming, include `client_request_id` in the resumed stream connect call; 3) ledger: support aliasing prov_keys so finalize can target aliases.

ben: For the ledger aliasing we can store prov_key parent pointers: when session B resumes from A we create alias prov:c-B -> prov:c-A. Finalize(prov:c-A) will scan aliases and mark them finalized. Need to be careful with scale though.

kevin: Perf note: scanning aliases on finalize might be expensive for high-throughput paths. Instead we can write finalization to a small join table: finalize_targets(prov_key) -> canonical_key. Canonicalization is set at resume time. Lookups are O(1).

sara: UX + telemetry actions: I can add a console filter that groups by canonical_request_id, and also surface a small telemetry counter: `charges_merged_on_resume` so we can measure how often this actually happens.

omar: Agreement on action items: short-term (low risk): group provisional lines in console and add telemetry. medium (eng-runtime): accept client_request_id + canonicalization, router to set canonical on resume. long-term (ledger): efficient alias table + atomic finalize.

ops-bot: @deploy scheduled: staging patch for console grouping pushed to canary at 2024-09-20T18:00Z :rocket:

ben: One more thing — tests. Need an integration test that simulates: toolcall_start (conn A), disconnect, resume (conn B) with explicit req_id and with implicit resume (no req_id) to validate both code paths.

marta: I'll own the integration tests + runtime changes. @sara please own the console grouping. @ben and @kevin we'll pair on the ledger aliasing design.

omar: Thanks all. Filing a follow-up RFC with detailed key formats and expected invariants.

sara: Added a short support note draft for CS explaining what customers will see and how we are fixing it — avoids 1:1 escalations. :+1:
